(1) the ionization fields of BCDs, pure starbursts, typical starbursts, AGNs, and starbursts with an AGN can be differentiated using the diagnostic diagram of [O iv]/[Ne iii] versus [Ne iii][S iii]; and (2) the BCDs and starbursts display higher [Ne iii]/[Ne ii] and [S iv]/[S iii] line ratios than the AGNs.
the ionization field in BCDs is similar to that of pure starbursts, but is stronger than that of AGNs.
the ionization field in BCDs is similar to that of starbursts but with a harder radiation field.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ionization field and its effect on the mid-infrared spectrum in extreme starbursts and AGNs.
the excitation of the ionizing field and the ionizing photon fluxes of the extreme starbursts, which is of great importance for our understanding of the evolution of galaxies and the origin of AGNs.
the excitation of the extreme starbursts, which are the progenitors of luminous infrared galaxies and quasars.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ionization field in BCDs is more intense than in typical starbursts but not as extreme as that of AGNs, and the difference is mainly due to a higher ionizing photon density in BCDs.
, although the excitation of the ionized gas in BCDs is similar to that in starbursts, the extreme conditions in BCDs can produce ionization levels comparable to AGNs.
the ionization field produced in a BCD is not identical to that of a typical starburst or AGN, but it is intermediate between the two, and it is more closely related to that of a low-luminosity AGN.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mid-infrared line ratios of BCDs and starbursts are consistent with their optical properties.
BCDs are not as extreme starbursts as once thought.
the ionizing spectrum of BCDs is similar to that of starbursts, but with a harder radiation field, and the difference between BCDs and AGNs is not as significant as previously thought.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ionization field produced by a starburst can be very similar to that of AGNs, especially in BCDs.
the mid-infrared spectra of BCDs are similar to those of pure starbursts but with stronger [Ne iii], [S iii], and [S iii] emission.
the ionizing field of BCDs is more extreme than that of starbursts and can be even more intense than that produced by an AGN.
